_comment: Decisions about a tournament number that changed, on the terms of ADR-0012. Each entry names one number, one of Sackmann's 2016-20 M-codes, or one exact id, and the number the event is filed under; `name` pins a display name where the latest edition's would mislead. Never for a name: a run joined by name is the rule's job and the page says so. Applied by `cmd/ingest -stage events`; an entry that files no row is reported.

overrides.note: Australian Open: Sackmann filed the women's Slams under the men's numbers 2016-21; Tennismylife uses the WTA's.
Roland Garros, as above.

Budapest: 1097 in 2017-19, 2036 from 2021. 578 is a second Budapest event of 2022-23 and stays apart.
Guadalajara: 2002 in 2019-21, 2075 from 2022.
Abu Dhabi: 2028 in 2021, 2088 from 2023.
Los Angeles 1984 Olympics: the id is the year until 1996, then 96 stays.

Sydney 2016-19: the name is under 338 (1969-2015), 3941 (1970) and 9663 (2022); the International is 338.

Rio de Janeiro 2016: the Rio Open, 6932 from 2014; 215 is 1989-90.
Adelaide 2020: the returned International, 8998 from 2022; 339 was the old one to 2008.

The WTA's year-end championships, 1975-2013: Virginia Slims, Avon, WTA Tour Championships, WTA Championships. No number until 2014, so each edition is named; 2014-15 bridge on their own. The ATP's equivalent is one number since 1970.
